name: Executive order of September 6, 1873 enlarging the Puyallup reservation
citation: Executive Order of September 6, 1873 (Royce, see area 405)
promises: Not a treaty. The President enlarged the Puyallup reserve set apart by executive order of January 20, 1857.
Royce says the enlargement covered only fractional section 34, T. 21 N., R. 3 E., too small to map, and that the reserve as enlarged was the Puyallup reserve of his day.
today: An enlargement, not a taking. No court or claims finding about this order was located.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule pp. 864-865

openQuestions: treaties.json names the tribe "Niskwali" and the present-day tribe as the Nisqually Indian Tribe; Royce lists "Niskwali and others", but the order enlarges the Puyallup reservation, so the Puyallup Tribe is the nation concerned. Not edited.
The Nisqually claim (ICC Docket 197) concerns the Medicine Creek treaty cession, not this order.
